rationale: The verification finding depends on a count whose sources are broader than the set its target describes, and the question a reader will ask next is whether that is a one-off or a pattern. Answering it needs no new reading beyond what is already cited, so it fits in the time left: the election path asks only voters for votes and tallies only those replies, the pre-vote path likewise asks voters only, the commitment calculation collects match indexes only for voters when the commitment is built and updated, the leader lease counts a contact only for servers whose suffrage is voter, and the verification is the single count that draws on anything else. I record that as one behaviour with the cited sites so the boundary of the finding is explicit: the defect is specific to leader verification, and a future reader does not have to re-audit four other paths to know it. No execution is spent and nothing else is added.

knowledge.statement: Auditing every quorum-like count in this package against the set its target is computed over leaves one mismatch and four matches. The mismatch is the leader verification, which credits the leader with a vote before consulting any configuration and counts acknowledgements from every entry of the replication state, non-voting members included, while its target counts voters only. The matches are: the election, which asks only voters for votes and tallies only those replies, with the quorum target computed over voters; the pre-vote, which likewise asks voters only; the commitment calculation, whose match map is built and rebuilt from voter entries alone, so acknowledgements from other members cannot enter it; and the leader lease, which records a contact only for servers whose suffrage is voter. Commit, election, pre-vote and lease therefore all compare a voter-derived count against a voter-derived target.
knowledge.conditions: This revision, the counts as written in the cited sites; the audit covers the quorum-like counts used for election, pre-vote, commitment and lease decisions, and does not cover message tallies that are not compared against a target.
